swap.text: Tycho Brahe ("TY-co BRAH-hay") was a successor of Copernicus. Although he died when his bladder burst on a carriage ride, his data helped this man formulate his three laws of planetary motion.
swap.clue: In 1615, this scientist defended his mother for 6 years in a witchcraft trial. This astronomer had earlier defied Church doctrine by claiming that the planets move in ellipses, not circles, as the first in his three laws of planetary motion.

question.leadin: Give the following about early Protestantism.
question.text: Luther's break from the Catholic Church began this period of religious history, in which Protestants tried to change the workings of the church.
question.clue: The Council of Trent codified the "Counter-" response to this movement, whose early proponents criticized the sale of indulgences.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Beer Hall Putsch.
swap.text: The Beer Hall Putsch happened in this city. This capital of Bavaria was also the site of the 1972 Summer Olympics, where 12 Israeli athletes were murdered.

question.text: Bismark was a proponent of this policy, which aimed to curb the power of the Catholic Church through a set of restrictive May Laws. This policy's name was coined by Rudolf Virchow, and it was implemented by Minister of Religion and Education Adalbert Falk.
question.clue: This social conflict came to an end with the passage of the First Mitigation Law negotiated following the death of Pius IX ], allowing clerics to be exempt from some Prussian laws.

swap.text: This final president of the republic allowed the Nazis to take power in 1933 by suspending civil liberties after the Reichstag Fire and transferring power to the cabinet with the Enabling Act.
swap.clue: This man was reviled by Hitler, who referred to him as "that old fool" and "that old reactionary" during his time as president of the Weimar ] Republic.

question.text: After Hitler was convicted and sent to jail, he sure had a lot of time to write this autobiography, in which he included his experiences with his parents.
question.clue: Volume 1 of this work was published while the author was in prison for attempting to overthrow the government of his nation.

swap.leadin: Name some responses to World War I.
swap.text: The War Guilt Clause contributed to the destabilization of this interwar German government, named for the city where its constitution was drafted.

question.leadin: The film The Lives of Others mentions a government attempt to conceal high suicide rates in this country.
question.text: Name this country, whose high suicide rates were linked to repression by a secret police led by Erich Mielke.
question.answerHtml: East Germany [accept Ostdeutschland accept DDR or GDR; accept German Democratic Republic or Deutsche Demokratische Republik; prompt on Germany or Deutschland] (The secret police is the Stasi.)
question.clue: This country's secret police, the Stasi, was formed while Walter Ulbricht was in power.

swap.leadin: This man worked with Gerhard Johann David von Scharnhorst to reform the Prussian army after he was released from captivity following the Battle of Jena (YEN-ah).
swap.text: Identify this general who led the Military Academy at Berlin from 1818 to 1830. This man's best known text advocated fighting decisive battles to completely defeat the enemy.
swap.answerHtml: Carl von Clausewitz [or Carl Philipp Gottlieb von Clausewitz]
swap.clue: This man noted that three quarters of combat operations were conducted under uncertain conditions.

swap.text: Among the various construction projects that Ludwig undertook was this castle, which is located close to the Hohenschwangau Castle where Ludwig grew up. Ludwig was inspired by the Singers' Hall of Wartburg Castle when cooking up his plans for this castle.

question.text: This nun recorded the visions she had in three books starting with the Liber Scivias. Known as the "Sibyl of the Rhine," she also composed one of the oldest musical dramas, Ordo Virtutum.

swap.leadin: Name these poets who took prominent roles in European politics.
swap.text: This poet, regarded as the second-most famous European behind Napoleon in his life, maintained a public stance of skepticism against German nationalism through the Napoleonic Wars. He also wrote Faust.
swap.clue: This writer described Kellermann's charge with the words "a new epoch in the history of the world has begun." This writer contributed such German classics as Faust and The Sorrows of Young Werther.

question.text: After World War I, Trebitsch took part in this failed 1920 counter-revolutionary coup against the Weimar Republic, during which he met Adolf Hitler. Walther von Luttwitz ("VAHL-tuh vahn LEET-vihts") was the primary coordinator of this coup.
question.clue: This 1920 coup against the Weimar government was supported by the right-wing Freikorps. It was defeated by a general strike, which in turn developed into a left-wing uprising in the Ruhr region.

swap.leadin: This victory for the Sixth Coalition followed Marshal Oudinot's failure to capture Berlin, setting up this culmination of the Trachenberg Plan.

swap.clue: The arrival of reinforcements the next day under General von Bennigsen and Prince Charles John helped to turn the tide of this battle, which also defection of Saxon troops under Jean Raynier.

question.leadin: The best known leader of this group was Klaus Stortebeker, and they became known as the Likedeelers after their wartime activities subsided.
question.text: Name these pirates that supplied food to the besieged city of Stockholm. They operated in the Baltic Sea from about 1390 to 1440, at the behest of the Dukes of Mecklenburg in their war against Denmark.
question.clue: They had their base at the city of Visby, but, after it was captured, many of their members became known as Likedeelers and allied themselves with East Frisian tribesmen.

question.leadin: This man's forces won a critical victory at the Battle of Tanga, which saw swarms of bees descend on the attackers on the slopes of Kilimanjaro.

swap.leadin: FTPE, name these German aces of the First World War.
swap.text: His 80 kills led all aces during war, though he did not survive it; his famed red Fokker triplane was downed in April 1918, with both Australian anti-aircraft gunners and Canadian pilot Roy Brown claiming credit.
swap.answerHtml: Manfred von Richthofen (prompt on Red Baron; prompt on Richthofen alone, as Manfred's brother Lothar was also a WWI ace)
swap.clue: Barnstormers often performed in groups called Flying Circuses. This nobleman led a fighter pilot squadron in World War I nicknamed the Flying Circus.
